sources: docs/plan/FINAL (WP dependency tables and acceptance text)
scope: One entry per OPEN_BUILDABLE, BUILT_NOT_SHIPPED and OPEN_NEEDS_DECISION item of items-A.json (341) and items-B.json (368), plus the slices of items cut into parts (slice_of / slices): 715 entries in all. SHIPPED, OWNER_ONLY and SUPERSEDED items are not here (see STATUS.md).

definitions.id: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens: the source id lowercased (WP-INFRA-23b -> wp-infra-23b); also the folder name candidates/r1h/<id>/
definitions.done: true only when the record verifies (candidates/r1h/<id>/STATUS.json passes with the red and green runs, test and HANDOFF.md on disk; a decision record needs its delegated row; an umbrella needs every child done). Nothing is marked done on a claim.
definitions.wave: 1 = the first dispatch batch (30 entries, authored against the repository, pairwise independent: disjoint write sets, no depends_on between them; an entry of it stays listed when it is done); 2 = entries authored after it (authored_wave2.py, authored_slices.py); null = no authored acceptance yet
definitions.next_batch: the entries to dispatch now: the first 30 entries in order that have an authored acceptance (a wave), are not done, wait for no open entry and share no written path with an earlier member (computed by merge_status.py, re-checked by check_backlog.py)
definitions.closes_in_part: the entry closes only part of its plan item; the text names the entry that carries the rest, so nothing of the plan item is dropped
definitions.order: position in the list: open build entries first by wave, value tier (survival, legacy A-line, grade A, full A+, optional), status (built-not-shipped first), size, roadmap node; an entry never precedes its open dependencies; umbrellas and decision records after the build entries; done entries last
definitions.tier: the lowest path of docs/plan/FINAL/15-roadmap.json in which the entry's roadmap node carries work (survival < legacy-a-line < grade-a < full-a-plus; tranche P7 = optional)
definitions.depends_on: open entries that must be done first: the plan's dependency tables, "after/once" clauses of the survey step, the children of an umbrella, and wp-arch-09 for rebuild entries
definitions.needs_split: size L: slice into entries of at most M before dispatch (split_hint quotes the plan's own numbered steps); a slice is done when its own acceptance holds and the entry when every slice is
definitions.acceptance_basis: authored = written against the repository; otherwise the machine proof clause plus the survey next step and the plan acceptance, quoted

items.acceptance: Red first: tests/historian/export-places.test.mjs fails before the exporter exists. The same export as the units slice for places: one `places/<slug>.json` per place of data-src/geo/places.json that has at least one corpus passage linked by the place linkers of WP-HIST-14, at most three excerpts of at most 120 words each with citation, scan address, licence id and `reviewer: null`, deterministic and content-hashed, no excerpt that is not a verbatim substring of the cited report, no place whose coordinate conflict is unresolved presented with a chosen coordinate (the file carries each source value and `chosen: null`, as in places.json). The test reuses the units slice's checks (shared helper, not copied) and adds the place-linker precision figure that WP-HIST-14 measured; if that measurement is not on record the file says "unmeasured" and the item states it. Not closed before wp-hist-22-units.

items.title: Build, chunk groups, budgets and hash scheme: WP-ARCH-10 proper (slice of WP-ARCH-10)
reads: docs/plan/FINAL/03-source-rebuild-and-parity.md (WP-ARCH-10, section 4.6 chunk map and byte budgets)

decision.summary: Delegated, conservative: the entry wp-arch-09 is the foundation half of the plan's WP-ARCH-09 (layout, stack record, token module, strict base, workspace manifest, the request note for the root files); it is done when its record verifies, a

items.value: The rebuilt app cannot ship without a deterministic build, hashed names and byte budgets; it is the second half of WP-ARCH-10.
items.acceptance: Size L: slice into entries of at most M before dispatch (split_hint), each with its own red-first test. The plan's WP-ARCH-10 Fix and Accept, whole: one build command runs the data build, the map build, the Astro build, `mount-legacy`, `gen-netlify-config` and the gates and writes `deploy-manifest.json` (path to sha256 and size) and `version.json` (app, data, timeModel, sha; `builtAt` from the commit date so builds stay deterministic); chunk groups of plan section 4.6 with a `shared` chunk so lazy chunks never import the entry; `modulePreload.polyfill:false`; first-party source maps published `noindex`; `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt`; `assert-hashed-assets.mjs` compares names with the last production manifest (manifest compare plus double build, because Vite's `[hash]` is not the sha256 of the file); `verify-deploy.mjs` (every referenced asset exists with exact case, no orphans); `/assets/*` and `/data/v2/*` immutable only once these gates exist. Accept: one patched byte without a rename fails CI; double build identical; no lazy chunk imports the entry; `size-limit` fails on a 5 percent rise of a chunk budget of section 4.6 (brotli, per chunk), and a budget raise needs a `budget-raise` label and an ADR. Nothing in release/R1g/dist changes.
items.short: Size L, slice before dispatch: deterministic one-command build with deploy-manifest.json and version.json, chunk groups with a shared chunk, hashed-name and deploy gates, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES, size-limit budgets that fail on +5 percent; double build identical.
items.owed: Real-device timing and the clean CI run are owed (owner-enabled CI); budgets are measured as bytes only.
split_hint: (a) build driver: deterministic build command, deploy-manifest.json, version.json (builtAt from the commit date), mount-legacy and gen-netlify-config hooks; double build identical
(b) gates: assert-hashed-assets.mjs against the last production manifest, verify-deploy.mjs (referenced assets exist with exact case, no orphans), one patched byte without a rename fails
(c) chunk groups and budgets: section 4.6 chunk map with a shared chunk, modulePreload.polyfill false, source maps noindex, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt, size-limit per chunk failing at +5 percent

items.title: Foundation half of WP-ARCH-09 (layout, stack record, Mapbox token module, strict base, workspace manifest): close the record

decision.summary: Delegated, conservative: the plan's packages/<name> is src/lib/<name> (src/lib/time already is) and apps/web is src/app; tests of a new area sit beside its code; the repository's own lockfile means npm stays the package manager (the plan na

items.value: Foundation of the whole rebuild chain (WP-ARCH-10..33): until a workspace, layout and config module exist, nothing else of the rebuild can start.
items.acceptance: Layout: packages/<name> of the plan maps to src/lib/<name> (src/lib/time exists) and apps/web to src/app; tests of new areas sit beside the code (src/<area>/tests) because tests/ is shared; this mapping is recorded in src/STACK.md with the stack choices that the register fixes (React 18.3.1 exact per row A10, Mapbox GL behind a facade, strict TypeScript for new files, Node 24 for the toolchain with the container default 22.23.4 still able to run every test of this workstream) and each choice the register leaves open is written as "not decided: owner" with the conservative default and the way back. `src/config/mapbox.js` is the one config module of the map token: it reads PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN, throws a named error when it is unset in a production build, embeds no token literal, and is the only reader of that variable (the test greps src/ for /pk\.eyJ/ and for other readers of the variable: both must be empty/absent), src/tsconfig.base.json is strict, and `node --test src/config/tokens.test.mjs` passes. A private src/package.json (workspaces ["lib/*", "app"]) is created; the root package.json is not in this workstream and stays untouched: the exact two-line change that wires the workspace is written as a request note (docs/battle-theatre/GOVERNANCE/horde/requests/main-site-wp-arch-09.md); no dependency is installed in this item. Red first: tokens.test.mjs fails before src/config/mapbox.js exists. `node --test tests/time/*.test.mjs` stays green (src/lib/time unchanged). State on 2026-11-14: everything above is built and was re-checked by the merge (src/config/tokens.test.mjs and src/foundation.test.mjs: 23 of 23 on Node 22.23.4 and on 24.22.1; red-first logs candidates/r1h/wp-arch-09/red-first.log and red-first-foundation.log; the request note exists). What is left is the record, because candidates/r1h/wp-arch-09/STATUS.json holds notes only: `tools/horde/bench.sh node candidates/r1h/_lib/record.mjs wp-arch-09 --test "node --test src/config/tokens.test.mjs src/foundation.test.mjs" --test "/opt/node24/bin/node --test src/config/tokens.test.mjs src/foundation.test.mjs" --test "node --test tests/time/*.test.mjs" --red-cmd "node --test src/config/tokens.test.mjs" --red-exit 1 --red-log candidates/r1h/wp-arch-09/red-first.log --files <the files of this entry that exist>` must exit 0 (STATUS.json then holds the tests, the red-first record and passes true, with the notes kept). This entry closes the foundation half of the plan's WP-ARCH-09; the half that is not built (pinned installs, lint, style and dead-code tools, the one-day toolchain smoke) is entry wp-arch-10-toolchain, so nothing of WP-ARCH-09 is dropped.
items.short: Built and re-checked (23 of 23 tests on Node 22 and 24): only the record is left. Run record.mjs through the lock with the three test commands (tests/time included) and the red-first log (command in the entry). Closes the foundation half; the toolchain half is wp-arch-10-toolchain.
items.owed: Clean-install CI (`install --frozen-lockfile && build && test`) needs the owner-enabled CI; token rotation is an owner step.
items.closes_in_part: Foundation half of WP-ARCH-09 only (layout, stack record, token module, strict base, workspace manifest, request note). The unbuilt half of the plan Fix (pinned installs, lint, style and dead-code tools, one-day toolchain smoke) is entry wp-arch-10-toolchain; browserslist, es-check and the WebGL2 gate stub are entry wp-dec-12.
